purpose: Fixes the 8 PWA/offline audit findings from issue #187: push-subscription churn, auth-sensitive API responses persisting in the service-worker runtime cache (plus a LOGOUT cache purge), a no-op connectivity poll, the network toast covering the top nav, a dead offline-retry code path, a stale committed sw.js artifact, swallowed install failures, and a missing offline image fallback.
riskRationale: No critical or security issues; the push-churn, LOGOUT-purge, and artifact-drift fixes are correct and cleanly integrated. Two important runtime defects remain: the offline image placeholder points at a URL that is never precached so the feature silently never works, and the new NetworkOnly rule omits /api/v1/health so the connectivity probe can be satisfied from the SW runtime cache and report 'online' while offline — the same coverage gap leaves other authenticated /api/v1 endpoints cached. All are small, isolated, auto-fixable changes.

text: A well-scoped, root-cause-driven PWA/offline hardening PR: stable useCallback identity plus a once-per-user ref guard for push subscribe, a NetworkOnly rule plus LOGOUT cache purge for auth data, a real health probe with an abort timeout, a repositioned network toast, a working intended-destination offline retry, removal of the drift-prone committed sw.js artifact, and install-failure error feedback. However, two of the claimed fixes do not work at runtime: the image fallback points at the wrong precache URL, and the health probe can be answered from the SW's own runtime cache — and the NetworkOnly denylist still leaves several authenticated /api/v1 endpoints cached. Recommend fixing these before merge.

reasoning: Two important, deterministic issues remain before merge: the offline image fallback references '/offline-placeholder.svg' while the asset is precached at '/icons/offline-placeholder.svg', and the /api/v1/health probe can be served from the SW's NetworkFirst cache so it reports 'online' while offline — the same incomplete NetworkOnly rule also keeps other authenticated endpoints cached. Each fix is a small, safe code change.

message: Prepending a NetworkOnly rule ahead of defaultCache for auth-sensitive endpoints is the right first-match-wins design, and pairing it with a LOGOUT handler that purges every non-precache cache (covering both legacy and current cache names) is solid defense-in-depth for cross-session data leakage.

Wrapping subscribe/unsubscribe in useCallback with accurate dependency arrays, combined with the once-per-user ref guard in PushSubscriber, gives them stable identity and correctly eliminates the per-render unsubscribe/re-subscribe churn the audit flagged.

The GET_INTENDED_DESTINATION message channel with a graceful router.back() fallback is a clean, working replacement for the dead sessionStorage branch, and the SW records the original navigation URL rather than the fallback page URL.
Repositioning the toast below the sticky TopNav and lowering z-index to z-20 is correct — TopNav is sticky z-30, so the indicator can no longer be covered by it.

Deleting the git-tracked build artifact and gitignoring it prevents the committed SW from drifting from app/sw.ts source; verification that the compiled sw omits skipWaiting preserves the AppUpdatePrompt update flow.
Replacing the empty catch with console.error, Sentry.captureException, and a destructive toast gives users and operators real feedback instead of silently swallowing install failures.

The image fallback url '/offline-placeholder.svg' does not match the actual asset, which lives at public/icons/offline-placeholder.svg and is precached as '/icons/offline-placeholder.svg'. Serwist's fallback resolves object entries via matchPrecache(url), which does an exact precache-key lookup, so it returns undefined and the placeholder is never served — broken-image icons persist offline, the exact scenario this finding was meant to fix.
suggestion: Point the fallback url at the actual precached path '/icons/offline-placeholder.svg' (or move the file to public/offline-placeholder.svg) so matchPrecache resolves a precache entry.

message: The NetworkOnly rule is incomplete. It omits /api/v1/health, so the connectivity probe in NetworkStatusIndicator.tsx:52 can be answered from defaultCache's NetworkFirst 'api' cache (a cached 200 served when the network fetch fails), reporting 'online' while actually offline — defeating the fix's stated purpose. The same gap means other authenticated /api/v1 endpoints (events, opportunities, volunteers, admin, youth-profiles, applications, etc.) are still persisted in the runtime cache, leaving user-scoped/PII data cached and making the audit's 'authenticated data in the SW cache' concern only partially resolved.
suggestion: Invert the rule — route all same-origin GET /api/v1/* requests through NetworkOnly by default, allowing only explicitly public endpoints to be runtime-cached. This both excludes /api/v1/health (so the probe always reaches the real network) and makes future sensitive endpoints safe by default. The minimal alternative is adding /api/v1/health to the existing matcher.

message: The once-per-user ref guard is only set by the auto-subscribe effect, not by handleSubscribe. When a user taps 'Enable' (permission goes 'default' -> 'granted'), handleSubscribe calls subscribe() and the permission change re-fires the auto-subscribe effect, which finds the guard unset and calls subscribe() again — each call unsubscribes and re-subscribes, so the very churn this PR targets still occurs once on the manual opt-in path.
suggestion: Also set the guard inside handleSubscribe before calling subscribe() so the follow-up auto-subscribe effect is a no-op for the same user+permission.

message: The LOGOUT message is only posted to navigator.serviceWorker.controller, which is null on first page load and whenever the controlling SW is waiting during an update (skipWaiting is intentionally omitted), so the cache purge can be silently dropped and previously cached authenticated data survives across sessions.
suggestion: Fall back to navigator.serviceWorker.getRegistration().then(r => r?.active?.postMessage({ type: 'LOGOUT' })) when controller is null so the purge reliably runs.

message: The GET_INTENDED_DESTINATION async body runs without event.waitUntil, so the browser may terminate the service worker before cache.match resolves and the INTENDED_DESTINATION reply is posted; the /offline page then falls back to router.back() instead of retrying the intended URL.
suggestion: Wrap the async reply in event.waitUntil(...) and consider having the offline page retry the GET_INTENDED_DESTINATION request a few times before giving up.

message: The ref guard is set before subscribe() resolves, so a failed background auto-subscribe (transient network/VAPID error) is never retried for the rest of the session — the user only gets another chance via an explicit prompt interaction.
suggestion: On subscribe() rejection, clear the guard so a later permission/user change or component remount can retry the background subscription.

message: The 5s probe timeout is aggressive for /api/v1/health, which performs a DB query and the HF Spaces backend can cold-start slowly; a slow-but-alive backend can exceed 5s and flash the 'Connection Lost' banner every cycle, a false offline state.
suggestion: Raise the abort timeout to match the 10s interval and/or only downgrade to offline after N consecutive probe failures to avoid transient false negatives.
